citation: Glessner House Museum, 'John M. Van Osdel, Chicago's First Architect', The Story of a House (blog), 31 August 2015; with an undated photograph of the Fernando Jones house, 1834 S. Prairie Avenue, photographer and holder not named.
author: Glessner House Museum

access_notes: Read 2026-10-19 (T-2642) from the live page; the photograph read from the image store's copy, 675 x 506 px, sha256 4180b8c58b74f7611529056a55633e18f01a35f37ad769ebda8bfefeff219283, which the page shows.
note: Read: Van Osdel designed two houses on Prairie Avenue; 'The first of these, at 1834 S. Prairie Avenue, was built in 1866 for one of Chicago's earliest pioneers - Fernando Jones'; 'The Italianate style house was razed in 1942.' The photograph, from across the street, shows the house before its 1886 mansard: two storeys of brick on a high stone basement, deep eaves on paired carved brackets, a low pediment-like gable with a round window over the middle of the front, tall windows under curved stone hoods, a one-storey angled bay at one front corner, and a stoop with iron railings.
what_it_supplies: the style, the architect and the year built
that the house was razed in 1942
the front as it stood before 1886: brackets, centre gable, window hoods, corner bay, stoop
what_it_does_not_supply: the 1904 roofline: the photograph predates the mansard
